text:
Tom Wilson's week was about a hit, not a goal. He was ejected for boarding Florida's Sandis Vilmanis, avoided a suspension, and Florida Hockey Now argued that was the wrong call. Wilson, to RMNB: "I was trying to make a north-south hit." Vilmanis has since returned.

On the ice, the 32-year-old is in the coldest stretch of a fine career: no goals in 14 games on 4.3 expected, and one point in his last ten. Two goals on 5.8 expected for the season, after scoring 30 last year. Our read is that it's some of each: the chances have dipped a little, and the ones he's getting aren't going in. Washington still takes 55% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, which says the rest of his game is intact.

Evolving-Hockey had him in the 90th percentile for driving play and the 99th for taking chances away last season, and better by chance quality than by goals. That's not a player who's lost it. Our talent range still has him near 20 goals. He's played 925 games for one franchise, won a Cup in 2018 and plays hard minutes. The goals usually come back to players getting these looks.
